title: Window for a Sum of Two Sine Waves
originalTopic: Period and amplitude bounds for a trigonometric sum
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: To display the complete shape of f(x) = sin x + sin 3x exactly once, what viewing window should be used? Justify the x-length from the period and the y-length from an amplitude bound.

steps.title: Find the period of the sum
steps.explanation: Both terms repeat after 2*pi, and 2*pi is the smallest common multiple of the individual periods 2*pi and 2*pi/3, so the sum has period 2*pi.
steps.why: An x-window one full period long shows the complete pattern without drawing the same feature twice.

steps.title: Bound the amplitude
steps.explanation: Each sine contributes at most 1, so the curve never leaves the horizontal strip between -2 and 2; factoring as 2 sin 2x cos x confirms the actual peaks stay below 2.
steps.why: A rigorous upper bound means the y-window can be chosen a priori instead of by trial and error on the screen.

steps.title: State the window with margin
steps.explanation: Using [0, 2*pi] by [-2.5, 2.5] frames one full cycle, the zeros at the multiples of pi/2 visible inside it, and enough vertical slack that the crests do not graze the frame.
steps.why: Padding the theoretical bound 2 to 2.5 keeps the local maxima from being clipped by pixel rounding.
